newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Nato-Ukraine formally agree security pact.
newsitem.headline: Nato-Ukraine formally agree security pact.

text.p: NATO and Ukraine on Thursday initialled a security pact, similar to a historic charter signed with Russia earlier this week, which tightens ties between the ex-member of the Soviet Union and its former foes in the western alliance.

"This is a very important document that is the result of three years of discussion," said Ukrainian Foreign Minister Hennady Udovenko after initialling the accord at a special ceremony during a NATO ministerial meeting here.
The pact will be formally signed by NATO heads of state and Ukraine at a summit meeting of the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO) in Madrid in July.

The charter gives Ukraine the right to call for "consultations" with NATO states if it feels threatened. It is intended to give the huge former Soviet republic a more weighty relationship with the alliance than that being granted to most other East European states.
But it does not go quite as far as the landmark security deal signed with Russian President Boris Yeltsin on Tuesday in Paris setting up a permanent NATO-Russian Council.
"It is a type of status symbol, which takes account of their size and importance," said one NATO diplomat.
